title: Round-trip test harness: property-based tests, golden vectors, and open-corpus round-trip
context: Reversibility is a tested property, not a marketing assertion. The harness proves round-trip fidelity using three independent methods: (1) golden vectors (curated input/output pairs from open authoritative examples), (2) property-based round-trip tests using fast-check over the script's Unicode ranges, and (3) open-corpus round-trip tests using a PD/CC corpus. For strict schemes the test asserts reverse(forward(s)) == NFC(s) for every input; the harness must fail CI on any regression. This harness is the trust foundation for all subsequent scheme data tasks.
objective: Build a test harness in the pnpm test pipeline that: loads golden vectors from data/vectors/<scheme-id>/, runs property-based round-trip tests (fast-check) over Unicode ranges for each scheme's source script, runs open-corpus round-trip tests on a PD/CC corpus, and asserts reverse(forward(s)) == NFC(s) for strict schemes. For normalized schemes, asserts round-trip equality up to the documented normalization contract. Does NOT assert round-trip equality for lossy schemes (only runs a loss-report smoke check).
acceptanceCriteria: Golden-vector runner: loads data/vectors/<scheme-id>/*.yaml (or .json), runs each input through the engine, asserts output matches expected; failures are reported per-vector with clear diff

Property-based round-trip (fast-check): generates valid grapheme sequences over the scheme's source-script Unicode ranges and asserts reverse(forward(s)) == NFC(s) for strict schemes; runs at least 1,000 generated cases per scheme

Open-corpus round-trip: runs a PD/CC corpus file (e.g., UDHR translation or Wikisource excerpt) through forward+inverse and asserts recovery per scheme class; corpus file(s) stored in data/corpora/ with license attribution
For normalized schemes: round-trip asserts equality up to the declared normalization contract (documented per scheme), not byte-identity
For lossy schemes: harness does NOT assert round-trip equality; instead runs a smoke check that a loss report exists and is non-empty
All harness failures exit non-zero and print actionable diagnostics; integrated into pnpm test
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint passes (with at least one stub scheme/vector to exercise the harness paths)
resources: PLAN.md — Reversibility section (three proof methods); Success metrics (round-trip fidelity definition)
output: packages/core/src/harness/ or packages/harness/ test runner; data/corpora/ with at least one PD corpus excerpt and license file; integration in pnpm test
